author: Brené Brown

coreIdeas.mentalMove: Readers can stop treating vulnerability as public exposure and start using it as careful contact with safe people.
coreIdeas.name: ordinary courage with compassion
coreIdeas.oneSentence: Small truthful speech weakens shame when it is shared with someone who has earned trust.

coreIdeas.mentalMove: Readers can notice when fitting in has replaced being known and can stop using approval as proof of worth.
coreIdeas.name: worthiness before performance
coreIdeas.oneSentence: Love and belonging require a stable sense that a person is enough before approval arrives.

coreIdeas.mentalMove: Readers can respond to painful exposure without turning one moment into a total self-condemnation.
coreIdeas.name: shame resilience
coreIdeas.oneSentence: Shame resilience means recognizing shame, separating it from guilt, speaking it with empathy, and owning the story before it owns behavior.

coreIdeas.mentalMove: Readers gain a way to notice when a room is asking for an edited self and can choose a truer response.
coreIdeas.name: authenticity as choice
coreIdeas.oneSentence: Authenticity is a repeated choice to let values and real identity guide behavior when approval pressure is present.

coreIdeas.mentalMove: Readers can repair errors without making flawlessness the price of belonging.
coreIdeas.name: self-compassion over perfectionism
coreIdeas.oneSentence: Self-compassion meets mistakes with kindness, common humanity, and mindful honesty instead of using shame as discipline.
